Drustvar (/ˈdrʌst.vɑɹ/ DRUHST-vahr) is the westernmost region of Kul Tiras. Heavily forested and mountainous, Drustvar is more inhospitable than neighboring lands, and produces most of the kingdom's ore as well as some of its toughest warriors. It is the seat of power for House Waycrest, one of four noble houses that rule Kul Tiras. As the original home of the Drust vrykul, the region witnessed intense fighting as the first humans of the Arathorian Empire battled to colonize the islands. Its legacy remains both dark and sinister, and has resurfaced in modern times in the form of perverse witchcraft and twisted cults.
The people of Drustvar have a deep hunting tradition, which includes a group of local rangers, while the Waycrest Guard employs falconers. Unlike the rest of Kul Tiras, which worships the Tidemother and the sea, the primary religion in Drustvar seems to be the worship of the Holy Light. It was described as a rugged land with a dark history and superstitious people.

A talking cat!}} It was described as a rugged land with a dark history and superstitious people.[[Drustvar (quest)]] ==History== ===Early history=== {{Main|Drust-human war}} [[File:Gol Osigr.jpg|thumb|The [[Drust]] ruins of [[Gol Osigr]] near [[Mount Cortis]].]] After the [[Great Sundering]] in 10,000 [[BDP]], various [[vrykul]] [[tribe]]s set out for the seas, and one such population, known as the [[Drust]], settled across the archipelago of [[Kul Tiras]].{{Ref web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8nGnT6WZbeI|title=Blizzcon 2018 Interview: Alex Afrasiabi & Patrick Dawson - Story and Systems | The Lost Codex|author=The Lost Codex|work=YouTube|date=2018-11-03|accessdate=2018-11-03}} Across Drustvar, [[Stormsong Valley]], and [[Tiragarde Sound]], they beat back the forces that threatened the land, including the great sea beasts and [[naga]], then built roads and structures in the areas they inhabited.{{Ref WoWCV4|133}} Around 2,700 BDP, [[human]]s from the [[Arathor|Arathorian Empire]] expanded their territory to the island, which they would later call Kul Tiras.{{Ref WoWCV1|133}} When the settlers tried for peace with the Drust, the latter went to war immediately,[[Pieces of History]] and aggressively launched raids against the humans' fledgling hamlets from Drustvar.[[The Ruins of Gol Var]] The assaults carried on for many years, until the ancestors of [[House Waycrest]] decided something had to be done, and eventually began a [[Drust-human war|war]] against the Drust. Seeking a way to counter the Drust's [[Necromantic|death magic]], the Waycrests founded the [[Order of Embers]] to fight them,[[The Order of Embers]] while the [[Thornspeakers]] [[druid]]s broke off from their barbarous people, and eventually integrated into Kul Tiran society.[[Ulfar#Quotes|Ulfar's gossip]] At the end of the war, [[Arom Waycrest|Colonel Arom Waycrest]] organized a final assault against the Drust and their city of [[Gol Osigr]],{{Ref WoWCV4|133|134}} assisted by both [[Ulfar]]'s Thornspeakers and [[Athair]].[[Besieged Villager]] After he defeated [[Gorak Tul|King Gorak Tul]], Arom was given the title of Lord and from then on, his family would rule Drustvar as House Waycrest.[[Clear Victory]] After the battle, Athair told Lord Arom that to repay the kindness he had shown to him, and that as long as he exists, he would protect the people of Drustvar should they come for his help. Ever since then, the valiant and true have found shelter with the White Stag of the forest.[[Besieged Villager]]s telling a story to the [[Besieged Village Child]]. The Thornspeakers once tended to Drustvar as kin of the trees, but that age has long since passed.[[Lost in the Woods]] ===Battle for Azeroth=== {{Bfa-section}} {{Main|Drust incursion}} [[File:Cursed Effigy.jpg|thumb|left|[[Fallhaven]] cursed by the [[Heartsbane Coven]].]] By the time of the [[Fourth War]] in 33 ADP, Drustvar was controlled by [[Lord Arthur Waycrest|Lord Arthur]] and [[Lady Meredith Waycrest]], who had gone suspiciously absent. In their absence, Drustvar's contributions of arms (and sausages) began to dry up until the [[Alliance]] [[adventurer]]s worked with their Kul Tiran allies to get to the bottom of the mystery, as well as the curse over the land.2017-11-03, [http://warcraft.blizzpro.com/2017/11/03/wow-battle-for-azeroth-new-continents-zones-blizzcon-2017/ WOW: BATTLE FOR AZEROTH NEW CONTINENTS, ZONES, BLIZZCON 2017]. ''Blizzpro'', retrieved on 2017-04-11 Unbeknownst to the Admiralty, Lady Meredith, stricken with grief due to her ailing husband, had called out to any power that could save him. It was [[Gorak Tul]] himself who answered her cry and promised that death would never part the couple,[[Lord and Lady Waycrest#Adventure Guide]] only if she began to recruit new members for the [[Heartsbane Coven]], which would bring the [[Drust]] back to the realm of the living.[[A Little 'Pick Me Up']] After adapting to their newfound powers, the [[witch]]es started to kidnap the local populace and take them to [[Waycrest Manor]], until the entirety of [[Corlain]] was under their control.[[The Fall of Corlain (quest)]] After he was informed by [[Priscilla Ashvane]] that the Waycrests were falling into a state of disrepair, [[Harlan Sweete]] sent [[Captain Leadfist]] to establish a base at [[Chandlery Wharf]]. Their objectives were to deplete the Waycrest's supplies, keep them destabilized, and prevent them from being able to support the [[House Proudmoore|Proudmoores]], while filling the Irontide's coffers at the same time.[[Sweete's Orders]] [[Anyport]] also fell under the control of [[Richard Tornsail]] and the Irontides, until the heroes helped [[Cesi Loosecannon]] defeat the [[pirate]]s and become the new boss of the smugglers' cove.[[An Economic Opportunity]][[Out With the Old Boss]] When [[wicker construct]]s attacked the small town of [[Fletcher's Hollow]], the populace was desperate to restore order and turned against [[Lucille Waycrest|Lucille]], the daughter of Lord and Lady Waycrest.[[The Waycrest Daughter]] Accused of being a witch, the townsfolk nearly hanged her at [[Hangman's Point]] until the Alliance ambassador, who had just saved [[Fallhaven]] from the Coven's curse,[[The Final Effigy]] arrived to clear her name.[[The Burden of Proof]] After the heroes rallied Fletcher's Hollow's woodsmen, fended off the wicker constructs, and evacuated the town, [[Constable Henry Framer]] received a letter from [[Evelyn Pare|Mayor Evelyn Pare]] exonerating Lucille.[[An Airtight Alibi]]{{Ref WoWCV4|134}} [[File:Arom's Stand.jpg|thumb|[[Arom's Stand]], headquarters of the [[Order of Embers]].]] Upon learning from [[Marshal Everit Reade]] that the witches had spread unchecked through Drustvar, recruiting women from the villages to join their ranks and binding spirits to wicker thralls,[[And Justice For All]] Lucille and the Alliance ambassador investigated the ancient [[Necromantic|death magic]] of the Drust. Within the ruins of [[Gol Var]],[[The Ruins of Gol Var]] they uncovered the secrets of the [[Order of Embers]], and eventually created a new generation of [[Inquisitor (occupation)|inquisitors]].[[The Order of Embers]][[A New Order]] During their assault on [[Waycrest Manor]], Lucille and her allies fought against the Heartsbane Coven, as well as Lord and Lady Waycrest, who had been turned undead.[[Waycrest Manor: The Fallen Mother]] When their deaths opened a portal to the realm of [[Thros, the Blighted Lands|Thros]], allowing Gorak Tul to return to the living world, the Alliance heroes rallied for one final push to thwart the Drust King's efforts. In the aftermath, Lucille Waycrast assumed her role as Lady of House Waycrest, appointed [[Joan Cleardawn]] as the new Marshal of the [[Waycrest Guard]],[[Everburning]] and later pledged the support of her house to [[Lord Admiral]] [[Jaina Proudmoore]].[[A Nation United (quest)]]{{Ref WoWCV4|135}} Aboard ''[[The Banshee's Wail]]'', [[Trade-prince]] [[Jastor Gallywix]] led the Horde's expedition into Drustvar, seeking to exploit the large amount of [[Azerite]] beneath the region.[[Drustvar Ho!]] The [[Bilgewater Cartel]] eventually settled [[Krazzlefrazz Outpost]] and began their mining operation, collecting silver within the [[Bleak Hills Mine]] and Azerite from [[Arom's Crossing]].[[Precious Metals (Horde)]] From the ''[[Strider (gunship)|Strider]]'' airship, [[Gelbin Mekkatorque|High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque]] eventually led an attack on the mining operations in Drustvar, using an army of remote-controlled robots.[[Test Case 1; Mech vs. Mekkatorque]] During the [[Faction Assault on Drustvar|Faction Assaults]] on Drustvar, the [[Order of Embers]] fought alongside the [[Purified]] against the [[Horde]], protecting the region and its inhabitants.[[In Every Dark Corner]] Both Fletcher's Hollow and [[Carver's Harbor]] were occasionally attacked by [[Darktide]] [[naga]], who amassed prisoners to sacrifice to their [[N'Zoth|dark master]], before being defeated by the adventurers.[[Naga Attack!]] ===After the Fourth War=== [[File:Gol Inath.jpg|thumb|[[Gol Inath]] in the [[Crimson Forest]], once used by the Coven to access [[Thros, the Blighted Lands]].]] Despite the defeat of the [[Heartsbane Coven]], the threat of [[witch]]es in Drustvar did not cease. By the time of the [[war against the Jailer]] in 35 ADP, some remained active in Drustvar and were still present at [[Gol Inath]], protecting the [[Flame of Oblivion]] under the orders of [[Gorak Zhar]], which contained a portion of Gorak Tul's power.[[Into the Flame]] In Year 40 ADP, [[Joan Cleardawn|Marshal Joan Cleardawn]] visited the [[T&W Trading Post]] in [[Stormwind City]] to buy new weaponry, as the Drustvar garrison were still fighting against the witches and were in need of anything useful against them.[[Trading Post#Stormwind]] In Year 42 [[ADP]], however, [[Taelia Fordragon]] mentioned that there were no otherworldly witches in Kul Tiras anymore,[[Taelia Fordragon#WoW's Anniversary]] revealing that the Heartsbane's threat had finally been vanquished. ===Exploring Azeroth=== {{Novel-section}} In Year 42 ADP, [[Lor'themar Theron]] arrived at Drustvar as part of his exploration of [[Kul Tiras]], and reminisced about how Drustvar was once terrorized by the coven of witches steeped in death magic. He visited several settlements and landmarks throughout the area and documented the information for [[Thalyssra]].''[[Exploring Azeroth: Islands & Isles]]'', pg. 106 The city of [[Corlain]] had been retaken from the [[Heartsbane Coven]], and [[Waycrest Manor]] was opened as a house once more under the guidance of [[Lucille Waycrest|Lady Lucille Waycrest]], who prioritized destroying all remnants and records of the [[witch]]es' work rather than remodeling her home. While the effects of [[Necromantic|death magic]] had left an imprint on the atmosphere, however, the city itself was thought of as downright cheery compared to how it was before the fall of the Coven.''[[Exploring Azeroth: Islands & Isles]]'', pg. 108 Other settlements, such as [[Fletcher's Hollow]], were reported as back to normal,''[[Exploring Azeroth: Islands & Isles]]'', pg. 113 while [[Fallhaven]] had recovered well; now bustling with tradesfolk and a newly opened ceramics kiln, though some of the locals were still wary.''[[Exploring Azeroth: Islands & Isles]]'', pg. 110 The [[Crimson Forest]] was now considered safe, but the local farmers still do not often venture inside. The Drust ruins and the entrance to the Blighted Lands had been destroyed and burned to ash, respectively.''[[Exploring Azeroth: Islands & Isles]]'', pg. 112 ==Official preview== [[File:Drustvar concept art.jpg|thumb|Drustvar concept art.]] In the land of Drustvar, the stalwart protectors of House Waycrest hold fast along the western border, but recently all contact with them has been lost. Travel beyond the frontier to learn of their fate and battle the resurgence of an ancient and terrifying enemy. Drustvar is a region known for the tenacity of the soldiers who protect it. Long after the defeat of the mysterious Drust who once dwelled there, the descendants of Arom Waycrest and his people continue to eke out a living in this unyielding land. They are known throughout Kul Tiras as being a hearty, stoic, and deeply superstitious people, and would make keen allies in the fight against the Horde—but now it's up to you to discover why they've gone silent. ;Welcome to Drustvar [[File:Drustvar 1.jpg|thumb|left|The sinister woods of Drustvar.]] When first arriving in Drustvar, you'll be greeted by a dark and foreboding shoreline on the eastern border. Drustvar is a rugged land plagued by superstition, and signs of witchcraft are everywhere. The pathways through Glenbrook to Fallhaven are fraught with danger, so you'll need to stay on your guard. Dark rumors swirl as to what may have befallen the Waycrest family—and if the Alliance has any hope of convincing the Kul Tirans to join them, you'll need to untangle the mysteries that lay ahead. Verdigris roofs and awnings adorn buildings of brick and wood, their amber window panes alight from within. The sea's intrinsic role in Kul Tiran culture is reflected in the architecture, and anchors and other symbols of the sea decorate doorways and awnings. A stygian pallor looms over the town of Fallhaven, reeking of mystical meddling. A large and ominous construct stands as sentinel in the center of town, and the townsfolk are... unresponsive. You'll need to work diligently to break the curse on the town before you can make any progress toward getting to the heart of the troubles in Drustvar. Cobblestone paths wind through the region and in and out of the various villages and towns. History and culture are deeply woven into the fabric of Kul Tiras, but so too are the workings of dark witches. Cursed and hopelessly twisted townsfolk and creatures work in servitude to these mystics' machinations, set to a task you'll need to decipher and put an end to—if you have the stomach for it. Visitors to this region will need to rely on their wits, solve a few not-so-small issues the citizenry faces, and hopefully make some inroads with the people along the way. There are more mysteries to unravel, and an ancient enemy is stirring in the land, causing a tremendous slew of trouble. ;Take the Highroad [[File:Drustvar 2.jpg|thumb|The cold mountains of Drustvar.]] Traveling westward will lead to a large chain of rugged snow-touched mountains running from the northern border of the region to the southern Iceveil Glacier, nearly bisecting the region in two. Along Highroad Pass, you'll come across various wildlife and creatures, including Chillwind Yetis who find the cold of the mountains to their liking and food sources plentiful. The road is fraught with danger, but you'll eventually arrive in the town of Arom's Stand, which overlooks a valley to the west. A tribute to Arom Waycrest stands vigil even as the people here struggle against the darkness that has swept over the land. On the southwestern coast, you'll cross into the Crimson Forest. Various shades of red assail your eyes and bear witness to the veracity of the name. The town of Falconhurst sits on the coast, and as in your previous travels through the region, you'll find this settlement is under siege by dark forces. ;Tainted Rule North of the Crimson Forest, the Ashenwood Grove bears witness to creatures adorned with fungi and strange creatures known as Fungarians patrolling the pathways. Farms dot the area and mines can be found dug into the mountainsides, but what should be bustling enterprises have ground to a halt as the witches' special brand of pestilent creatures wreak havoc. Each clue found and mystery solved only puts forth more questions as to what could be ultimately manipulating events in Drustvar. Perhaps you'll find the source of the troubles within Waycrest Manor—ancestral home of the Waycrest family who watches over Drustvar. A vast coastline surrounds Drustvar to the east, south, and west, where those brave enough can fish, boat, swim, and hunt for treasure. Inland, the mountains and forests provide a chance to hunt a variety of... interesting... creatures. To the north, the rolling hills and mountains of Stormsong Valley await, while eastward lies Tiragarde Sound—and even more opportunities to earn your way into the good graces of the Kul There are also [[Drustvar Trader|traders]] from the area. *One of the ships of the [[Lost Fleet|Third Fleet]] was the ''[[Drustvaria]]''. *There is a bar in [[Anyport]] called [[The Drust Bar]]. *In life the [[Defenders of Drustvar]] were valiant champions who had sworn to protect the land and its people.[[Split Party]] *[[Bloodfly|Bloodflies]] are a type of [[Fly|flies]] found in Drustvar known to bite people. According to a story, they don't bite a [[witch]] because they wouldn't touch her foul blood.[[Trial by Superstition]] *There are many sausage vendors in Drustvar or hailing from the area, such as [[Charisse Payton]] and [[Elijah Eggleton]], a cultural note acknowledged by the [[Sausage Sampler]] achievement. Even [[Brennadam Citizen]]s reminisce about them. *The cut quest [[Thesis Statement]] had someone (likely from the [[Adventurer's Society]]) hypothesizing that there were [[titan]]ic ruins under Drustvar because of the presence of [[trogg]]s.[[Thesis Paper Page]] *In its earliest stages of development, Drustvar was planned to be a cold, frozen zone in northern Kul Tiras with the witches as only a small part of the story.[[BlizzCon 2017]], ''Battle for Azeroth'' Demo | Drustvar Zone *During alpha and beta, the adjective for something related to Drustvar was "Drustvari". ==Gallery== File:Anyport.jpg|[[Anyport]] File:Barrowknoll Cemetery.png|[[Barrowknoll Cemetery]] File:Carver's Harbor.png|[[Carver's Harbor]] File:Corlain.jpg|[[Corlain]] File:Corlain 2.jpg|[[Upper Corlain]] File:Lower Corlain.jpg|Lower Corlain File:Chandlery Wharf.png|[[Chandlery Wharf]] File:Falconhurst.jpg|[[Falconhurst]] File:Fallhaven.png|[[Fallhaven]] File:Fletcher's Hollow.png|[[Fletcher's Hollow]] File:Glenbrook Homestead.jpg|[[Glenbrook Homestead]] File:Gol Koval.jpg|[[Gol Koval]] File:Hangman's Point.jpg|[[Hangman's Point]] File:Krazzlefrazz Outpost.png|[[Krazzlefrazz Outpost]] File:Mount Cortis.jpg|[[Mount Cortis]] File:Swiftwind Post.png|[[Swiftwind Post]] File:Ulfar's Den.jpg|[[Ulfar's Den]] File:Western Watch.png|[[Western Watch]] File:Whitegrove Chapel front.jpg|[[Whitegrove Chapel]] ==Patch changes== *{{Patch 9.1.5|note=Level range changed to 20-50.}} *{{Patch 9.0.1|note=Level range changed to 25-50 (was 110-120).}} *{{Patch 8.0.1|note=Added.}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Elinks-zone|8721}} {{Drustvar}} {{Kul Tiras}} [[Category:Drustvar| ]] [[Category:Kul Tiras]]
